name: Navigating Your Second-Story Addition Timeline

step.name: Step 1: Step 1: Initial Assessment & Feasibility (2–4 weeks) — This is wher…
step.text: Step 1: Initial Assessment & Feasibility (2–4 weeks) — This is where we first check if a second story is even viable. We'll look at your existing foundation, walls, and framing to see if they can support another level. We also verify zoning and height restrictions. This step involves a preliminary structural assessment to identify potential challenges early on.

step.name: Step 2: Step 2: Design & Engineering (6–12 weeks) — Once feasibility is con…
step.text: Step 2: Design & Engineering (6–12 weeks) — Once feasibility is confirmed, an architect or designer creates detailed plans, considering egress, building envelope, and how the new story integrates. A structural engineer steps in to design the new floor, load paths, roof, and any necessary reinforcements. This ensures everything is sound and meets code.

step.name: Step 3: Step 3: Permit Review & Acquisition (4–16 weeks) — All the architec…
step.text: Step 3: Permit Review & Acquisition (4–16 weeks) — All the architectural, structural, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, and energy documents are submitted to your local building department. This phase can take a while, as jurisdictions have varying review times and may require responses to plan-check comments before issuing approvals.

step.name: Step 4: Step 4: Demolition & Temporary Weather Protection (2–4 weeks) — Wit…
step.text: Step 4: Demolition & Temporary Weather Protection (2–4 weeks) — With permits in hand, we safely remove the existing roof and prepare the structure. Crucially, your home is protected from the elements during this period with robust temporary weather barriers to prevent damage.

step.name: Step 5: Step 5: Framing & Rough-ins (8–16 weeks) — This is where your new s…
step.text: Step 5: Framing & Rough-ins (8–16 weeks) — This is where your new story really takes shape! The new floor and wall framing go up, followed by the installation of new plumbing, electrical, and HVAC lines. This phase includes multiple inspections by local authorities to ensure everything meets code.

step.name: Step 6: Step 6: Enclosure & Finishes (8–12 weeks) — Once rough-ins pass ins…
step.text: Step 6: Enclosure & Finishes (8–12 weeks) — Once rough-ins pass inspection, the exterior of the new story is enclosed, making it weatherproof. Inside, we install insulation, drywall, flooring, trim, and all the fixtures and finishes that bring your vision to life.

step.name: Step 7: Step 7: Final Inspections & Approval (1–2 weeks) — The project culm…
step.text: Step 7: Final Inspections & Approval (1–2 weeks) — The project culminates with final inspections from the building department. Once everything is approved, you get the green light to enjoy your beautiful new second story!
